activities.tooltip: Loads a configuration workbook into a dictionary, from a local file or an Orchestrator storage bucket.

args.t: Where the config workbook lives. LocalFile reads from disk. StorageBucket downloads it from an Orchestrator storage bucket first.
Path to the config workbook. A full local path when Source is LocalFile; the file name inside the bucket when Source is StorageBucket.
Sheets to load as key/value settings. Defaults to Settings and Constants. The sheet named Assets is always read separately into Asset Names.
Orchestrator storage bucket holding the config workbook. Required when Source is StorageBucket.
Orchestrator folder the storage bucket belongs to, for example Finance/Production. Leave empty to use the robot's current folder.
All key/value pairs from the settings sheets, merged into one dictionary. Lookups are case-insensitive.
Logical name to Orchestrator asset name mapping, read from the Assets sheet.

activities.tooltip: Registers process identity fields so every later log line carries them automatically. Call once at init, and again per transaction to tag the transaction id.

args.t: Config dictionary. ProcessName, ClientName, BotType and Environment are read from it and registered as log fields.
Tags every subsequent log line with this transaction. Pass the queue item reference at the start of each iteration.

activities.tooltip: Writes a structured log entry through the robot's logging pipeline. Identity fields come from the log context, not from arguments.

args.t: Human-readable message. Name the record and the system: 'Ticket.Create failed for invoice INV-4471', not 'Error occurred'.
Log level. Info for milestones, Warn for recovered failures, Error for a failed transaction.
Where in the process this happened, for example ServiceNow.Ticket.Create. Becomes a queryable field so one search replaces a regex over free text.
Extra structured fields for this event only.

activities.tooltip: Reports how many of the named processes are running or pending, for use as a concurrency gate.

args.t: Release names to check.
Running jobs allowed before Limit Reached is true.
Ignore the job making this call. Leave true unless you specifically want to count yourself.
Orchestrator folder to check. Empty uses the robot's current folder.
True when the running count has reached Max Concurrent.
How many of the named processes are running or pending.
Which ones. Log these so a blocked start says what blocked it.

activities.tooltip: Returns true when a stop has been requested for this job from Orchestrator. Returns rather than throws, so the caller can finish the current transaction first.

args.t: True when Orchestrator has requested this job stop.

activities.tooltip: Retrieves one new transaction from an Orchestrator queue.

args.t: Queue to pull from.
Orchestrator folder holding the queue. Empty uses the robot's current folder.
Order transactions are taken in. In-progress items are deliberately not offered: retrieving one hands a second robot work another robot is already doing.
Return only items whose Reference starts with this value. Empty matches any.
The transaction. Nothing when none matched.
True when a transaction was returned. Branch on this to end the transaction loop.

activities.tooltip: Closes a transaction as successful or failed, with the failure classified so Orchestrator retries only what is worth retrying.

args.t: The transaction to close.
True marks the transaction Successful. False marks it Failed.
Application allows Orchestrator's automatic retries. Business does not. Required when Successful is false, and enforced at runtime.
Why it failed. Required when Successful is false, and enforced at runtime: a failed item with no reason cannot be triaged.
Orchestrator folder holding the queue. Empty uses the robot's current folder.
Data to attach to the transaction for reporting.

activities.tooltip: Returns a transaction to the queue AND increments its retry count, failing it permanently once the limit is reached. Re-queueing without counting is always a bug, so this does both.

args.t: The transaction to return to the queue.
Attempts allowed before the item is failed permanently.
Delay before the item becomes eligible again. Zero makes it immediately available.
Why it is being retried. Recorded on the item and written to the log.
Orchestrator folder holding the queue. Empty uses the robot's current folder.
Attempt number after this call.
True when the limit was reached and the item was failed instead of re-queued. The item is already closed: do not also call Resolve.

activities.tooltip: Merges values into a transaction's specific content without replacing the rest.

args.t: The transaction to update.
Keys to set on the transaction's specific content. Keys not supplied are left alone.
Replace the entire content instead of merging. Destructive: anything not in Values is lost.
Orchestrator folder holding the queue. Empty uses the robot's current folder.
True when the update was accepted.

activities.tooltip: Issues an HTTP request with timeout, retry on transient failures, and optional bearer authentication.

args.t: HTTP verb.
Full request URL including query string.
Sent as an Authorization bearer header. SecureString so it is never rendered into a log line, whatever the consuming process has configured.
Additional request headers.
Request body for POST, PUT and PATCH.
Request timeout. A call without one can block a robot indefinitely on a dead endpoint.
Attempts on transient failure: 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 and transport timeouts. 4xx other than 408 and 429 are never retried.
HTTP status of the final attempt.
Raw response body as text.
True for any 2xx status.

activities.tooltip: Creates a folder, including any missing parent folders.

args.t: Folder to create. Parent folders are created as needed.
Full resolved path, so a caller holding a relative path does not have to rebuild it.
True if the folder was created, false if it already existed.

activities.tooltip: Deletes files matching a pattern in a folder. Destructive: the pattern is required, so deleting everything has to be asked for explicitly.

args.t: Folder to delete from. Must exist.
Glob pattern, for example *.tmp. Required: pass * explicitly to delete everything in the folder.
Only delete files last modified more than this many days ago. Zero means no age filter.
Include subfolders.
How many files were deleted. A cleanup that removed 10,000 instead of 10 is only discoverable if the activity says so.
Full paths of every file deleted.

activities.tooltip: Generates a random password as a SecureString, plus a masked username safe to include in a notification.

args.t: Password length.
Characters allowed in addition to letters and digits.
Guarantee at least one uppercase, lowercase, digit and special character.
Username to mask for inclusion in a notification.
HEAD masks the first four characters, TAIL the last four, ENDS both, MIDDLE the centre.
The generated password. SecureString by design: there is no plaintext output, because a password that becomes a String can reach a log.
Masked form of the username, safe to put in an email body.

activities.tooltip: Acquires a Microsoft Graph access token using client credentials, cached in-process until shortly before expiry.

args.t: Logical name of the app registration. Resolved through config to a tenant id, client id and credential asset, so adding one is three config rows rather than a library release.
OAuth2 scope requested. Client-credentials flow against Graph requires .default: narrowing happens in Entra, not at call time.
Timeout for the token request.
Bypass the cache and mint a new token. Use only after a 401 on a call that should have succeeded.
Bearer token as a SecureString. Pass straight into an activity that accepts one; never convert it to String in a workflow.
UTC expiry of the returned token. Informational: the cache handles renewal, so do not branch on this.

activities.tooltip: Looks up an Entra ID user by email or user principal name and returns their profile.

args.t: Bearer token from Get Graph Token.
User principal name or mail address.
Graph $select fields. Defaults to displayName, givenName, surname, jobTitle, mail, mobilePhone, businessPhones, officeLocation, department and accountEnabled.
Request timeout.
The Graph user object. Empty when not found.
False when Graph returned 404. A missing user is a business outcome, not a system failure, so it does not throw.

activities.tooltip: Sends an email through Outlook 365, falling back to SMTP if the primary channel fails.

args.t: Outlook 365 connection from Integration Service. The primary send channel.
Recipients. At least one is required.
Subject line.
Message body. HTML is accepted.
CC recipients.
BCC recipients.
Full paths of files to attach. Verified before anything is sent, so a bad path fails cleanly rather than half-sending.
Message importance.
SMTP connection used only when the primary send fails. Leave empty to disable the fallback, in which case a primary failure throws.
True when the message was accepted by either channel.
Primary or Fallback. Fallback firing means the primary channel is degraded right now: alert on it.

activities.tooltip: Replies to an Outlook 365 message, optionally to all recipients.

args.t: Outlook 365 connection from Integration Service.
The message being replied to, as returned by Get Emails.
Reply body. HTML is accepted.
Reply to every recipient of the original rather than the sender alone.
Additional CC recipients beyond those carried over.
BCC recipients.
Full paths of files to attach. Verified before sending.
Message importance.
True when the reply was accepted.

activities.tooltip: Forwards an Outlook 365 message to one or more recipients.

args.t: Outlook 365 connection from Integration Service.
The message being forwarded, as returned by Get Emails.
Recipients of the forward. At least one is required.
Text placed above the forwarded content.
CC recipients.
BCC recipients.
Additional files to attach beyond those already on the message. Verified before sending.
Message importance.
True when the forward was accepted.

activities.tooltip: Finds a file in a SharePoint site or Teams document library and downloads it.

args.t: Full SharePoint URL of the site or team, copied straight from the browser address bar. For example https://contoso.sharepoint.com/teams/FinanceAutomation
Exact file name including extension. Matched case-insensitively.
Local folder or full file path to download to. A folder keeps SharePoint's own file name.
Folder within the document library. Leave empty for the root.
Document library name when the file is not in the default library.
Replace an existing local file. When false, an existing file causes an exception rather than a silent replace.
Timeout for the download.
Full local path of the downloaded file. Use this rather than rebuilding it from Save Path and File Name.
False when no matching file exists at that location. Not finding a file is a normal outcome and does not throw.

activities.tooltip: Creates a record in a ServiceNow table and returns both its sys_id and its display number.

args.t: ServiceNow instance for the REST call. Credentials for each instance are resolved from config.
Table to create the record in.

Field name to value. Common incident fields: short_description, description, assignment_group, caller_id, urgency, impact, category, state, work_notes. Reference fields take a sys_id, not a display name.
false returns database values, true display values, all both. Display values are slower because ServiceNow resolves them rather than reading them directly.
Request timeout.
sys_id of the created record. This is what Update Record and Get Related Tasks need.
Display number of the created record, for example INC0012345. This is what goes in a subject line or a log entry a human reads.
The full created record.

activities.tooltip: Retrieves one ServiceNow record by sys_id.

args.t: ServiceNow instance for the REST call.
Table to read from.
The record's 32-character sys_id. Not the display number: INC0012345 is a number, not a sys_id, and passing one returns nothing rather than an error.
Fields to return. Restricting these is the single biggest performance win on a wide table.
false returns database values, true display values, all both.
Request timeout.
The record. Empty when not found.
False when no record has that sys_id. A missing record does not throw, so a polling loop can continue.

activities.tooltip: Returns ServiceNow records matching an encoded query. Both the query and the limit are required, so an unfiltered request against production cannot be issued by accident.

args.t: ServiceNow instance for the REST call.
Table to query.
Encoded query, for example active=true^assignment_group=<sys_id>. Required: an unfiltered request returns up to ServiceNow's default limit of 10,000 records.
Maximum records to return. Required, because an unbounded query against a production instance is never intended.
Fields to return.
Field to sort by. Prefix with a minus sign for descending.
false returns database values, true display values, all both.
Request timeout.
Matching records.
Number of records returned. Equal to Limit means results were truncated, and a warning is logged.

activities.tooltip: Updates fields on an existing ServiceNow record.

args.t: ServiceNow instance for the REST call.
Table holding the record.
The record's 32-character sys_id, as returned by Create Record.
Fields to set. Only the fields supplied are changed. Common: state, work_notes, close_notes, close_code, assignment_group.
false returns database values, true display values, all both.
Request timeout.
The record after the update.
True when the update was accepted. Updating a record that does not exist throws rather than silently succeeding.

activities.tooltip: Returns the child tasks of a ServiceNow record.

args.t: ServiceNow instance for the REST call.
The parent record's 32-character sys_id, as returned by Create Record.
Request timeout.
Child task records. Empty when there are none.
Number of related tasks found.

activities.tooltip: Resolves ServiceNow user sys_ids to email addresses, and reports which ones did not resolve.

args.t: ServiceNow instance for the REST call.
sys_user sys_ids to resolve.
Request timeout.
sys_id to email address. Users with no email on record are absent.
sys_ids that did not resolve. Without this, 47 emails back from 50 users looks like success and three people silently stop being notified.

activities.tooltip: Expands ServiceNow groups to their member user sys_ids, deduplicated across groups.

args.t: ServiceNow instance for the REST call.
sys_user_group sys_ids to expand.
Exclude deactivated users. Leave true: paging people who have left fails silently.
Request timeout.
Distinct sys_user sys_ids across all groups. A user in two groups appears once.
Groups that resolved to no members, so an empty notification list is distinguishable from a mistyped group id.
